# Ezekiel 24 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** On January 15, in the ninth year of our exile, the LORD's message came to me:

**2** "Son of man, write down today's date — because this is the very day the king of Babylon has begun his siege against Jerusalem.

**3** Tell this parable to these rebellious people. Say to them: The Lord GOD says: Put the cooking pot on the fire. Set it there and pour water into it.

**4** Fill it with the best cuts of meat — the thigh, the shoulder. Pack it with choice bones.

**5** Use the best of the flock. Pile wood under the pot. Bring it to a rolling boil and cook the bones along with the meat."

**6** So the Lord GOD says: "How terrible it will be for this city of murderers! She is like a pot corroded with rust that can never be scrubbed clean. Take out the meat piece by piece — no sorting, no choosing.

**7** The blood of her murders is still in her midst. She splashed it on bare rock — she didn't even try to pour it on the ground and cover it with dirt.

**8** I have left her blood on bare rock, exposed for all to see, to fuel My anger and bring My vengeance.

**9** So the Lord GOD says: How terrible for this city of bloodshed! I will pile the fuel even higher!

**10** Pile on the wood! Light the fire! Cook the meat thoroughly! Mix in the spices! Let the bones char!

**11** Then set the empty pot on the coals until it glows red-hot, until the copper burns and the built-up filth melts away, until the corrosion is consumed.

**12** But it's useless — even fire can't clean this pot. The corrosion is too deep.

**13** Your filthiness is your lewdness. I tried to cleanse you, but you refused to be cleansed. So you will not be clean again until I have poured out My full fury on you.

**14** I, the LORD, have spoken. The time has come. I will act. I will not hold back. I will show no pity. I will not change My mind. You will be judged by your own conduct and your own actions, declares the Lord GOD."

**15** Then the LORD said to me:

**16** "Son of man, I am about to take away the person you love most — with a single blow. But you must not mourn. You must not cry. Don't let a single tear fall.

**17** Groan quietly. Don't observe any mourning customs for the dead. Keep your turban on and your sandals on your feet. Don't cover your face in grief. Don't eat the customary food of mourners."

**18** I spoke to the people that morning. That evening, my wife died. The next morning, I did exactly as I was told.

**19** The people asked me, "Won't you tell us what this means? Why are you acting like this?"

**20** So I told them, "The LORD gave me this message:

**21** 'Tell the people of Israel: The Lord GOD says: I am about to desecrate My own Temple — the fortress you are so proud of, the place you love to look at, the place your heart longs for. And the sons and daughters you left behind in Jerusalem will be killed by the sword.

**22** When that happens, you must do what Ezekiel has done. Don't cover your faces in mourning. Don't eat the mourners' bread.

**23** Keep your turbans on and your sandals on. Don't mourn. Don't weep. Instead, you will waste away because of your sins, groaning to each other.

**24** Ezekiel will be your sign. Everything he has done, you will do. When all this happens, you will know that I am the Lord GOD.'

**25** Son of man, on the day I take away their fortress — their beautiful joy, the delight of their eyes, the longing of their hearts — along with their sons and daughters,

**26** on that day a survivor will escape and come to you with the news.

**27** On that day, your mouth will be opened. You will talk with the survivor and be silent no more. You will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am the LORD."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **24:2**: Ezekiel is in Babylon, hundreds of miles away, and God tells him: 'Write down today's date — the siege of Jerusalem starts TODAY.' Real-time revelation across vast distance. The specificity is stunning.

- **24:16-18**: This is the most devastating moment in Ezekiel's life. God tells him, 'I'm going to take your wife tonight — and you are not allowed to grieve publicly.' Ezekiel's personal tragedy becomes a sermon. The cost of prophecy is staggering.

- **24:27**: For years, Ezekiel has been mostly silent — only speaking when God opens his mouth. When Jerusalem falls, his mouth will finally open. The prophet's silence is broken when the prophecy comes true. Everything he warned about has happened.

— PNEUMA
